question: Should OpenClaw accept local Codex rollout files as a permanent source of native patch diagnostics, or require a supported typed app-server contract?
rationale: The choice determines remote-runtime compatibility, ownership of sensitive transcript content, upgrade guarantees, and whether request-time filesystem inspection belongs in the projection path.

options.title: Require typed app-server diagnostics
options.body: Remove the rollout scanner and land the capability only after Codex exposes bounded failure details through a supported event or item field.

options.title: Accept the private rollout dependency
options.body: Keep the scanner only with explicit maintainer ownership of version compatibility, remote-runtime limitations, privacy, latency, and upgrade proof.

options.title: Pause this direction
options.body: Defer or close the branch until the upstream protocol can carry the required diagnostic detail safely.

recommendation.title: Require typed app-server diagnostics
recommendation.body: Remove the rollout scanner and land the capability only after Codex exposes bounded failure details through a supported event or item field.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history places this person closest to Codex app-server runtime integration and diagnostic-boundary decisions.
